It’s hardly necessary to say that IoT tools are being widely applied today in many industries and business sectors. Numerous solutions, from [fitness apps](https://www.cogniteq.com/sports-software/fitness-apps) to enterprise management systems, are enriched with features provided by IoT devices, or systems of smart sensors. But in this article, we’ll focus on another extremely important but less discussed sphere where the Internet of Things is of great value. We are talking about solutions for the social sector and, more precisely, IoT for seniors.

IoT for elderly care is one of the most promising developments for ensuring secure independent living for seniors. The value of such solutions enriched with IoT devices for elderly shouldn’t be underestimated, not only for seniors but also for families who worry about them but don’t have the ability to stay with them 24/7.

## IoT for seniors and other IoT solutions: Market overview

The [global IoT market volume](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/industry-reports/internet-of-things-iot-market-100307) hit $714.48 billion in 2024. It is expected that the market size will reach $4,062.34 billion in 2032. A projected CAGR for the period from 2025 to 2032 is over 24%.

![IoT for seniors and other IoT solutions: Market overview](https://content.cogniteq.com/s3fs-public/inline-images/The%20Global%20IoT%20Market%20Volume.png?VersionId=W5EYhF_uwmLQSx2nDQou3BMkBcRniFfo)

North America was the fastest-growing region in 2024.

Many solutions from the category of IoT elder care are related to medical care and supporting health and wellbeing. These solutions represent part of the Internet of Medical Things segment. (In a previously published article, we explain the capacities and [benefits of IoMT](https://www.cogniteq.com/blog/internet-medical-things-iomt-innovative-future-healthcare-industry). We suggest reading it if you are interested in learning more.)

This category also demonstrates stable growth. The volume of the IoMT market is expected to reach over [$2,294 billion](https://www.precedenceresearch.com/internet-of-medical-things-market) in 2034. Solutions targeted toward older people help increase the accuracy of diagnoses, improve remote monitoring of chronic diseases, enhance the patient experience and decrease operational costs for healthcare institutions.

The COVID-19 pandemic was one of the factors that spurred the adoption of smart solutions among elderly people.

According to [studies](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/mobile/) conducted by the Pew Research Center, 95% of people in the US aged 65 and older own a mobile phone, and of those, 78% are smartphones. These figures clearly indicate that mobile software solutions, including IoT apps, focused on seniors’ needs can be a very promising segment.

## Use cases of IoT for senior citizens

At the moment we can define three main types of solutions that could be included in the category of IoT for senior citizens, based on the tasks they perform.

![Devices](https://content.cogniteq.com/s3fs-public/inline-images/Devices_0.png)

- ### _**Security and safety for seniors**_


Many seniors live alone, without adult children close enough to help when needed. Though nothing can guarantee 100% safety, systems of connected smart devices can greatly enhance it.

Some IoT solutions are aimed at ensuring safety in living spaces. IoT devices can monitor temperature, air quality, and humidity in seniors’ apartments and flats and notify family members if a dangerous change is observed.

Other [smart home solutions](https://www.cogniteq.com/blog/iot-home-automation-solutions-smart-home) can be utilized in elderly care. For example, there are smart devices (with or without cameras) that can control door and window openings as well as detect unauthorized entries and movements and send notifications to an authority or security company. Employing such solutions can protect not only seniors but also their properties.

- ### _**Health state monitoring**_


Health is one of the most important aspects to focus on when speaking of solutions for the elderly. According to various studies, nearly 80% of elderly people have chronic diseases that require regular monitoring. Today there are many devices such as glucose meters and blood pressure monitors that help to track vital parameters.

Results from these smart devices are sent into the cloud, where they can be collected by a healthcare organization. This can help doctors detect any problems and analyze and respond to them in a timely and appropriate way. What’s more, it is possible to have the software automatically notify a medical worker if some parameter has reached a dangerous value.

A range of IoT solutions for older patients is available to deal with various diseases:

- _**Diabetes**_**.** These solutions are powered by connected blood sugar monitors. A wearable device can continuously measure the level of sugar and if a patient’s blood sugar level is low, doctors get an emergency alert.
- _**Arthritis**_**.** There are also smart devices that facilitate many tasks for seniors who experience joint pain and difficulties with movement. For example, there are smart lighting systems, smart door locks, etc. Other solutions are aimed at easing pain, for instance by using wearable devices that stimulate nerves.
- _**Heart diseases**_**.** Special wearables, such as heart rate monitors, can allow for continuous monitoring while seniors move about and carry on with their normal lives.
- _**Parkinson's disease**_**.** For doctors, it is important to know how the severity of patients’ symptoms changes during the day. Special IoT sensors can collect data about symptoms and send them to the cloud.
- _**Special needs**_**.** There is also a group of solutions designed for people with _vision_ or _hearing impairments_. They help seniors to support communication with others [despite their disabilities](https://www.cogniteq.com/blog/iot-people-disabilities-how-technology-makes-their-lives-better). Notable among these products are apps powered by smart devices that help translate text into Braille or solutions that decrease background noise and direct wanted sound into the ear canal.

One more issue many adults over 65% suffer from is falls. Falls may be caused by a variety of issues, including neurological disorders, problems with vision, cognition, etc. It may happen that after a fall, a person is not able to call for help. However, modern IoT solutions powered by sensors that can be placed in smart bracelets, belts, shoes, and watches can monitor the wearer’s location, detect falls and send a notification to an organization or individual.

Some solutions not only help people deal with the consequences of falls but also prevent falls in the first place. They analyze movement patterns, track location, and notify a person that there is a risk of a fall.

These solutions can be enriched with motion sensors that detect the wearer’s movements; if no movement is detected over a set time, an alert is sent out so that timely medical aid can be provided.

- ### _**Everyday tasks**_


Smart devices can change the way the elderly perform many tasks, from communication with medical staff and families to shopping. For example, thanks to smart speakers, seniors don’t even need to switch on their computers or open apps when they want to order groceries or something else.

## IoT devices for elderly care

As you can see, the range of elderly care IoT solutions is rather wide and, more importantly, is continuously expanding as more companies bring innovative ideas to market.

The growth of the market is possible thanks to the development of software products in tandem with advanced devices, including wearables, aimed at solving many tasks. Here are some of the most widely applied devices for IoT elder care:

- Smart home devices (smart blinds, fridges, lighting, thermostats, etc.)
- Medical connected devices (glucose meters,  blood pressure monitors, pill dispensers, oximeters)
- Wearables (smartwatch or bracelets)
- Smart speakers
- Cameras (with microphones and without)
- Sensors (motion sensors, biometric sensors, etc.)

## Challenges of IoT for Elderly Care

Implementing IoT for Elderly Care involves addressing several challenges to maximize its potential benefits:

### **Data Privacy and Security**

Ensuring the protection of sensitive health information is paramount.

### **Digital Divide**

Developing user-friendly interfaces for non-tech-savvy seniors to ensure accessibility.

### **Device Reliability**

Guaranteeing that IoT devices function correctly to maintain elderly safety.

### **System Integration**

Seamlessly incorporating smart elderly care solutions into existing healthcare systems for cohesive operation.

## Benefits of IoT for Elderly Care

The integration of IoT for Elderly Care has revolutionized how elderly care services are provided, enhancing the quality of life for seniors:

### **Continuous Health Monitoring**

IoT devices track vital signs and send real-time data to caregivers, ensuring prompt medical intervention.

### **Automated Daily Tasks**

Smart elderly care solutions automate medication reminders and home automation, promoting independence.

### **Cost Reduction**

Efficient management of chronic diseases through IoT reduces healthcare costs.

### **Enhanced Safety**

Real-time alerts from IoT devices improve elderly safety by quickly notifying caregivers of any issues.

### **Improved Quality of Care**

Personalized care plans based on data from IoT devices ensure that seniors receive tailored treatments.

### **Social Connectivity**

IoT devices can help seniors stay connected with family and friends through easy-to-use communication tools.

## Aging-in-place technology and the role of IoT

Aging-in-place is a term used to describe the ability of older adults to continue living safely and comfortably in their own homes as they age without the need to move to assisted living facilities.

Thanks to this approach, seniors can enjoy independence and emotional well-being while maintaining their routines and community connections.

**How IoT makes it possible**

IoT enables aging in place by combining continuous monitoring, automated home management, and enhanced safety. Here are the key aspects where it helps:

- _**Health monitoring**_. Wearable senior monitoring devices track vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure, activity levels, etc.) and send real-time data to family members and healthcare professionals.
- _**Smart home safety for elderly**_. Smart sensors can detect falls, unusual movement patterns, or changes in daily routines.
- _**Home automation.**_ Voice-activated assistants, smart thermostats, automated lighting, and connected door locks help seniors manage their homes easily and safely.
- _**Environmental awareness.**_ Sensors can monitor air quality, temperature, and other conditions, so that the home remains comfortable and safe.

## AI and ML in elderly care

The developments in AI and ML change the approach to processing huge volumes of data and allow making solutions for seniors more advanced and efficient.

Let’s consider the most common ML and AI use cases in elderly care.

### AI-powered healthcare monitoring

AI systems analyze data from wearables, smart sensors, and medical devices to detect abnormalities in various aspects and parameters, like sleep patterns and daily routines. This continuous insight helps caregivers and healthcare providers react quickly and prevent serious health problems.

### Predictive fall detection

ML models can identify patterns that signal an increased risk of falls, including slower walking speed or unusual movement trends. Instead of only reacting after an accident, predictive fall detection alerts caregivers in advance. This helps improve safety and reduce hospitalizations.

### Voice assistants for seniors

The role of voice assistants like Alexa and Google Assistant in supporting independence for older adults can’t be underestimated. Seniors can use simple voice commands to set medication reminders, control home appliances, check the weather, call family members, and execute a lot of other daily tasks. For individuals with limited mobility or vision impairment, voice-activated technology provides a new way to interact with the surroundings.

### Chatbot companions

AI-powered chatbots act as companions for seniors who struggle with social isolation. These conversational agents can engage in simple dialogue. They can remind users about daily routines, share news or stories, and provide emotional support. Chatbots can’t fully substitute human connection. But they help reduce loneliness and keep seniors mentally engaged.

### Predictive analytics

According to recent [reports](https://www.mcknightsseniorliving.com/news/senior-living-providers-have-concerns-about-interoperability-optimism-about-ai-survey-finds/), nearly 70% of senior living organizations rely on AI for predictive analytics. Such tools allow them to forecast health risks, as well as optimize staffing and personalize care plans. As a result, these organizations can offer smarter and more proactive support for aging populations.

## Future Trends in IoT for Elderly Care

The future oftheElderly Care industry looks promising with the integration of advanced technologies. The elderly care services will likely incorporate more sophisticated AI and machine learning algorithms to provide personalized care and predictive health analytics. We are expected to see an increase in wearable technology, offering continuous health monitoring with greater accuracy.

Additionally, innovations such as voice-activated assistants and smart home devices will become more prevalent, further enhancing elderly care services. These trends will ensure a more proactive approach to elderly safety and health management.

## FAQ

### How can IoT help seniors?

IoT for seniors is aimed at helping people in dealing with their everyday tasks as well as at ensuring safety and continuous health monitoring. There is a big group of home care solutions for patients with different chronic diseases.

### What is the future of technology for the elderly?

It is expected IoT for senior care will be greatly enriched with innovations and more advanced tech tools already in the nearest future. Among the most promising tendencies, we can name the introduction of more sophisticated AI algorithms that will help seniors to solve many tasks without the involvement of other people.

### What is AgeTech?

This term is used to describe technology solutions that are designed to support the aging population. Such solutions help seniors maintain independence and health, as they address the unique challenges of aging, including mobility, cognitive decline, chronic disease management, and social isolation. This group of solutions encompasses a wide range of tools, from smart home devices to telehealth platforms and AI-powered IoT healthcare for seniors.

### What does the term “aging in place” mean?

This notion refers to the ability of seniors to live safely and comfortably in their own homes as they age, instead of moving to assisted living or care facilities. Aging-in-place technology ensures independence and familiar surroundings for maintaining daily routines. Technologies like IoT, remote monitoring, and smart home devices play a key role in making this possible.

### How do IoT elderly care solutions help seniors live independently?

IoT for seniors provides continuous monitoring of health and home environments. Smart sensors, wearables, and connected devices perform a wide range of functions, including tracking vital signs, detecting falls, and managing medication reminders. IoT systems can also automate daily tasks. For example, they can be used to control lights, thermostats, and appliances. This gives seniors more control and, at the same time, reduces risks at home.

### What are the best IoT devices that I can buy for elderly parents?

If you are looking for helpful IoT devices for seniors, we recommend that you consider such options as wearable health trackers, fall detection sensors, smart pill dispensers, voice-activated assistants, or smart home security systems. When choosing devices for the elderly, pay attention to their ease of use, reliability, and compatibility with monitoring platforms.

### How much do smart home for seniors and elderly monitoring systems cost?

The cost of IoT elderly care solutions is influenced by numerous factors, including complexity and features. Prices for some basic devices like wearable trackers or smart sensors can range from $50 to $200 per unit. Meanwhile, comprehensive smart home systems or remote monitoring platforms can cost significantly more. Moreover, when you buy any devices of this kind, you should also check subscription fees for connected services or apps that can also be applied.

### Are IoT solutions safe for seniors with dementia?

The safety of such solutions depends on whether they are designed with simplicity and secure connectivity. Devices should minimize complex interactions and use automated monitoring instead of requiring constant input. This is crucial for users with dementia. However, the safety is also a responsibility of caregivers, who must ensure privacy and provide guidance to prevent confusion or misuse.

### Are strong tech skills required for using IoT devices?

No, even seniors with low tech skills can benefit from such solutions. Many IoT devices for elderly people have simple interfaces, voice controls, and automated functions. As a rule, elderly monitoring systems and smart home solutions require minimal technical knowledge. Good training and intuitive app design are among the key factors that boost the adoption of such technologies.

### How can IoT help family caregivers?

IoT solutions provide real-time monitoring and alerts, which reduces the need for constant physical supervision. Caregivers can track health metrics and receive notifications about medication adherence or unusual activity. This improves peace of mind and enables timely interventions.
